headline: Extends the National Alzheimer's Project through 2035, adds a focus on healthy aging, and expands its advisory council.
what_it_does: This law keeps the National Alzheimer's Project running through 2035. The project helps federal agencies coordinate their plans and programs on Alzheimer's disease and related dementias. The law adds a focus on healthy aging and on reducing risk factors linked to memory and thinking decline. It also adds new members to the Advisory Council on Alzheimer's Research, Care, and Services.

who_it_affects.group: People living with Alzheimer's disease or other dementias
who_it_affects.how: The federal planning effort on these conditions continues through 2035, and a person diagnosed with Alzheimer's will now sit on the advisory council.

who_it_affects.group: Older adults and people concerned about memory decline
who_it_affects.how: The national plan will now include work on healthy aging and lowering risk factors for cognitive decline.
The advisory council will add a researcher with experience recruiting and keeping diverse participants in clinical trials.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies such as the Department of Justice
who_it_affects.how: Representatives from more federal agencies will join the advisory council.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted October 1, 2024; the project is extended through 2035.
